kb_knowledge.short_description: How to reset or unlock your corporate password
kb_knowledge.keywords: password, reset, unlock, locked out, credentials
kb_knowledge.text: Self-service reset: visit https://id.acme-corp.example/reset and authenticate with your registered mobile device. Service desk procedure: verify the caller's identity with two pieces of non-public information, unlock the account in the identity console, then force a password change at next logon. Passwords must be at least 14 characters. After a password change, users must clear cached credentials in any VPN or mail client (see KB0000004).

kb_knowledge.short_description: VPN client installation and first-line troubleshooting
kb_knowledge.keywords: vpn, remote access, tunnel, client, install
kb_knowledge.text: Install the corporate VPN client from the software portal. First-line checks when a tunnel will not establish: confirm the user has internet connectivity, confirm the client version is 7.2 or later, confirm the account is not locked, and check the VPN-GW-01 status page for a maintenance window. If the tunnel establishes then drops repeatedly, capture the client log and escalate to Network Operations - repeated drops usually indicate an IKE rekey mismatch rather than a client fault.

kb_knowledge.short_description: Payment service runbook: 502 errors and gateway timeouts
kb_knowledge.text: Symptoms: checkout requests return HTTP 502 or time out. Step 1 - check the health endpoint on PAY-APP-01. Step 2 - check replication lag on PAY-DB-01; lag above 120 seconds will fail readiness probes and take nodes out of the pool. Step 3 - check connection pool saturation; exhaustion has previously caused intermittent timeouts and is resolved by raising the pool size and performing a rolling restart of the application pods. Step 4 - if the database is healthy, check SAN latency on the underlying storage before restarting anything. Always raise a P1 and follow the major incident process in KB0000008 when the error rate exceeds 25%.

kb_knowledge.short_description: VPN authentication failures after a password change
kb_knowledge.keywords: vpn, authentication, password change, cached credentials, keychain
kb_knowledge.text: When a user changes their corporate password, the VPN client continues to present the previous credentials from the local keychain and authentication fails. Resolution: open the VPN client, choose Forget Saved Credentials, remove the stored entry from the operating system keychain, then reconnect and enter the new password. This resolves the issue without any change on VPN-GW-01.

kb_knowledge.short_description: Requesting new hardware: laptops, monitors and peripherals
kb_knowledge.keywords: laptop, monitor, hardware, request, new starter, peripheral
kb_knowledge.text: Standard hardware is ordered through the service catalogue, not through an incident. New starter equipment requires five working days notice and line manager approval. Monitors and headsets are issued from local stock where available. If equipment is required sooner than five working days, the request must be approved by the department head.

kb_knowledge.short_description: Outlook mobile mail and calendar sync troubleshooting
kb_knowledge.keywords: outlook, email, mobile, sync, iphone, android, exchange
kb_knowledge.text: If mail stops syncing on a mobile device: confirm the device has network connectivity, confirm the mailbox is not over quota, remove and re-add the account in the mobile client, and confirm the device passes compliance checks in the mobile device management console. Devices that fail compliance after an operating system update are silently blocked from EXCHANGE-01 until they are re-enrolled.

kb_knowledge.short_description: Database replication lag: diagnosis and remediation
kb_knowledge.keywords: database, replication, lag, mysql, replica, performance
kb_knowledge.text: Check the replica status to obtain the current lag in seconds. Common causes are long-running transactions on the primary, single-threaded apply on the replica, and storage latency on the underlying datastore. If storage latency is elevated, escalate to IT Infrastructure before attempting any replica rebuild - rebuilding on a degraded array will make the situation worse.

kb_knowledge.short_description: Major incident process and P1 escalation policy
kb_knowledge.keywords: major incident, P1, escalation, priority, bridge, process
kb_knowledge.text: A major incident is any incident with impact 1 and urgency 1, or any incident affecting a service with business criticality '1 - most critical' for more than 30 minutes. The on-call major incident manager must be engaged within 15 minutes, a bridge opened, and customer-facing updates posted every 30 minutes. Only the major incident manager may downgrade the priority of a declared major incident.
